name: TripleKSampler (Wan 2.2 base + Lightning high/low)
plain: Three KSamplerAdvanced runs in a row, all with the same ModelSamplingSD3 shift. Stage 1 is the base high-noise model on a long schedule, stage 2 the Lightning high model, and stage 3 the Lightning low model on the short Lightning schedule. Stage 1's length is chosen so it ends at the same fraction of denoising as stage 2 starts (base_steps/total = lightning_start/lightning_steps), searching for integer pairs from a quality floor of 20 total steps. The high-to-low switch is at a step number, at 50%, or at the first step where the sigma drops below a boundary (T2V 0.875, I2V 0.9, or manual). 'Refined' strategies then nudge the shift in 0.01 steps until the switch step's sigma is closest to the boundary. Noise is added only at the first stage that runs, and later stages continue from the leftover noise. The Simple node fixes Lightning cfg to 1.
math:
Symbols: L lightning steps; s lightning_start; T total base steps; b base steps; α shift; β boundary.
Alignment: b/T = s/L (s=1: b = ⌈20/L⌉, T = b·L; else smallest T ≥ 20 with T·s ≡ 0 mod L).
Switch: w = first i ≥ 1 with timestep(σ_i)/1000 < β (else L−1); 50%: ⌈L/2⌉, or ⌊L/2⌋ for manual −1.
Stage 1: base, S_T steps 0..b. Stage 2: L-high, S_L steps s..w. Stage 3: L-low, S_L steps max(s,w)..L.
Refine: α ← α ± 0.01 until |S_L(α)[w] − β| stops falling.
